citation: USDA FoodData Central, Foundation Foods, release 2026-04-30
note-on-host: The download page advertises fdc-datasets.nal.usda.gov, which does not resolve. The file is served from fdc.nal.usda.gov/fdc-datasets/, the host tools/usda.mjs already uses for SR Legacy.
unit: g/100 g for beta-glucan, raffinose and stachyose; mg/100 g for ergothioneine. Per 100 g of the food as sold, which is this store's basis.
note:
Not SR Legacy. Foundation Foods is a separate and much smaller release of individually analysed samples, published with the number of samples, the minimum, maximum and median behind each figure, and the analytical method. It carries components SR Legacy defines and never fills: SR Legacy publishes zero rows of beta-glucan across 7,793 foods and this release has 199.

Every row below is a foundation_food, which is the released value. The release also contains 75,055 sub_sample_food rows, which are the individual laboratory subsamples behind those values and are not cited here.
what-else-is-in-it: Beyond the rows mapped here: beta-glucan for 199 foods, ergothioneine for 91, quinic acid for 144, boron for 844, MK-4 for 438, raffinose and stachyose for 18 each. Pectin and inulin are defined and empty. Most of the boron is dry beans labelled '(0% moisture)', which is a dry basis and is refused. Most of the quinic acid is fruit juice and most of the MK-4 is meat and cheese. The rest of this release has not been mapped and is the largest unworked seam this store has.

rows.note: The FoodOn annotation gives the species and no preparation, hence close rather than exact.
The only one of the three whose FoodOn annotation states the preparation: 'oyster mushroom (raw)'.

rows.food: Oats, whole grain, rolled, old fashioned
Soy milk, unsweetened, plain, shelf stable
rows.note: The first raffinose and stachyose figures here for a soy food that is drunk rather than cooked, which is why they sidestep the basis problem that blocks every cooked-legume source. Shelf stable where the page's soy milk is unqualified, hence close.

rows.why-unmapped: The page's oats are rolled and this release carries both, so the rolled row is the one that maps. Kept because the pair is the clearest evidence here that cut and rolled oats are not interchangeable for this component.
The page's barley is pearl barley, boiled. Flour is neither the same preparation nor the same water content.

rows.food: Crimini, portabella, maitake, enoki, king oyster, lion's mane, beech, pioppini
rows.why-unmapped: Eight further mushrooms carrying both beta-glucan and ergothioneine, none of them foods on this page. King oyster reaches 23.63 mg of ergothioneine and enoki 25.75, several times the shiitake figure, so this is where the column would grow if the page ever gained them.
